title: Functions, argument labels, closures and trailing closure syntax

videos.script: A function is a promise written in its first line. What goes in, and what comes out. {{functions}} You will write three for the planner, and see the compiler hold each one to its promise. {{labels}} Then something Swift does that most languages do not. Every parameter has two names. One for the call, one for the inside. The call ends up reading like a sentence. {{defaults}} Then defaults, for the usual case. And inout, for the rare function that changes your variable, with an ampersand to warn you. {{closures}} Then the turn this lesson is really about. A function is a value. You can store it, pass it, and write it with no name at all. {{trailing}} You will see that closure move outside the brackets, which is how most Swift code looks. {{capture}} Last, what a closure keeps alive after the function that made it has gone. By the end, the planner's arithmetic is in functions, and you can hand one function to another.
